correctness.rationale: Correct under the explicitly normalized radial complete-Pick criterion. Both factors have nonnegative positive-kernel expansions and are nonvanishing on the disk. For F=1-1/K the coefficients at n>=m+1 are c_n-tau c_(n-m), c_n=alpha Gamma(n-alpha)/[Gamma(1-alpha)Gamma(n+1)]; their ratio is the increasing product prod_{j=1}^m(n-j-alpha)/(n-j+1). Thus n=m+1 gives the necessary and sufficient all-degree cutoff, not a finite-experiment inference. The Hardy alpha=1 polynomial has negative degree m+1 for tau>0. The gamma ratio gives the claimed decay. Exact coefficient checks for nine rational (alpha,m) pairs independently verified the bound and first obstruction; exact nonconcavity diagonal equals 151/551>0. Normalizations, tau boundary and m>=2 were checked.

value.rationale: Motivated sharp stability boundary for Schur products of two separately complete-Pick kernels, a nontrivial kernel-property failure not captured by mere existence of a Pick factor. The degree-localized first obstruction, asymptotic decay and explicit distinction from concave shifts give structural information beyond a relabelled general criterion; narrow but natural family and all-order classification.

final_claim: For 0<alpha<=1, m>=2 and 0<=tau<=1, K(t)=(1-t)^(-alpha)/(1-tau t^m) is complete Nevanlinna–Pick precisely when tau<=prod_{j=1}^m(j-alpha)/(m+1)!. At threshold the degree m+1 reciprocal defect coefficient is zero and all other nonconstant coefficients are positive (for alpha<1); threshold decays like m^(-1-alpha)/Gamma(1-alpha). At alpha=1 only tau=0 works. The complete-Pick example (alpha,m,tau)=(1/2,2,1/10) has nonconcave multiplication by z.
limitations: Only 0<alpha<=1 and one sparse nonnegative resolvent factor tau<=1 on the unit disk; nonconcavity is one witness, not classification for all parameters.
